documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Routine recheck.

Winter went fine - one cold in February that her coworkers all had, got over it in a week without antibiotics. Energy back to her own normal now that the days are longer. Morning stiffness under an hour. Taking everything as listed; brought the pill organizer, matches our list.

Exam: vitals fine. Throat clear, no nodes. Lungs clear. Spleen tip palpable as before. Hands unchanged, no warm joints. Skin intact.

Plan: no changes. DXA at the fall wellness visit (4 years on risedronate). Usual labs with rheumatology's schedule. Reviewed when to call for fever.

documents.title: Filgrastim Coverage Renewal
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Specialty pharmacy called: filgrastim authorization expiring. Prescriber is hematology - called their office, they will submit the renewal. Patient informed she has two syringes at home, enough for now.

documents.title: Rheumatology Follow-up Letter
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body:
Date of visit: 06/13/2023

Patricia Kelleher, 55, seropositive RA since 2014, Felty syndrome.

Interval: stable. Stiffness 30-45 min daily. No flares requiring extra steroid. No infections requiring antibiotics.
Exam: chronic deformity at MCPs bilaterally with mild ulnar deviation; no tender or swollen joints on 28-joint count. Spleen not examined.
Medications: methotrexate 20 mg weekly; prednisone 5 mg daily; folic acid 1 mg; risedronate 35 mg weekly; calcium + D3; filgrastim prn.
Allergies: sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim - anaphylaxis; ibuprofen - gastropathy.

Assessment: low disease activity on current regimen.
Plan: continue. Labs every 3 months via PCP. Return 6 months.

Rheumatology

orders.order: DXA bone density, hip and spine

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Subsequent AWV.

No falls. Independent. Still at the library 12-15 hrs/week. PHQ-2 1. Cognition screen normal. Brought a health care proxy form, filed.

Health since last year: no infections needing treatment; filgrastim not used. Rheumatology June letter - low activity, no change. Hematology seen in winter per patient, no change (no letter received).

Exam: BP fine. Spleen tip palpable. Joints quiet with fixed hand changes. No kyphosis, no spinal tenderness.

Plan:
- DXA ordered, last 2019.
- Mammogram ordered.
- Tdap today (last >10 yrs per records).
- Flu/COVID at nurse visit next month when updated vaccine is out.
- CBC, CMP, vitamin D.
- Medicines unchanged.

reports.study: DXA bone density, hip and spine
reports.text: Indication: long-term glucocorticoid use, on bisphosphonate since 2019. L1-L4 lumbar spine T-score -2.6. Left femoral neck T-score -2.3. Comparison 06/2019 outside study: lumbar spine -2.7, femoral neck -2.4. No significant interval change at either site.
reports.conclusion: Osteoporosis, lumbar spine. Stable compared with 2019.

documents.title: DXA Result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Patricia - your bone density is essentially the same as 2019 (spine -2.6, hip -2.3). That means the risedronate is holding things steady while you stay on prednisone. Keep taking it and the calcium/vitamin D.

documents.body:
Rebooked from December.

Doing ok. Fatigue at her usual. Joints fine, stiffness about half an hour. No infections. Saw hematology in January, she says counts "the same as always".

Exam: well. Lungs clear. Spleen tip palpable. No synovitis. No bruises or petechiae.

A/P: stable on current regimen. Labs today for rheum. Recheck at fall AWV, sooner if needed.

documents.title: Hematology Follow-up Letter
documents.author: hematology
documents.body:
Visit: 06/18/2024

Diagnosis: Felty syndrome (seropositive RA, neutropenia, splenomegaly). Marrow 04/2021 hypocellular with maturation arrest; splenic FNA 05/2021 benign.

Since last visit no fevers or infections. Has not used filgrastim in over a year. Exam: spleen 1-2 cm below the costal margin. No lymphadenopathy.
CBC: WBC 2.8, ANC 1.3, Hgb 11.0, platelets 152 - stable.
Meds: methotrexate 20 mg weekly, prednisone 5 mg, folic acid, risedronate, calcium/D3, filgrastim 300 mcg prn ANC <1000.
Allergies: sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim (anaphylaxis), ibuprofen (gastropathy).

Plan: continue observation. Return in 6 months, sooner for infection.

Hematology & Oncology

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
AWV, 56 y/o.

Function intact. No falls. Lives alone, manages her own meds. PHQ-2 1. Cognition normal.
Hematology June: stable, letter reviewed.
Rheumatology: last seen spring per patient, regimen unchanged; letter not received.

Exam: unremarkable apart from palpable spleen tip and old RA hand changes.

Prevention: mammogram 11/2023 negative, next this winter. Pap 2022 negative with HPV, next 2027. Colonoscopy due 2028. Vaccines: flu and COVID next month. PCV20, zoster series, Tdap done.

Labs today. Medicines unchanged. Follow-up in about 3 months.

documents.title: Immunization Visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Trivalent flu vaccine L deltoid; 2024-25 COVID vaccine R deltoid. Observed, fine. Reminded to call for fever over 100.4 given her neutropenia.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here for worse tiredness over the last couple of months and hands that are stiffer and puffier in the mornings, now well over an hour before she can work buttons. Wrists ache. No fever, no infections, no bleeding. Taking methotrexate every Sunday, has not missed doses.

Exam: afebrile. Mild fullness over several MCPs and both wrists, a little tender, not hot. Spleen tip palpable. No bruising.

A/P:
1. Increased RA symptoms - sounds like more disease activity. She has a hematology appointment at the end of December already; rheumatology next opening is February. Message sent to rheumatology asking if they can see her sooner. Avoid NSAIDs (gastropathy).
2. Fatigue with Hgb 10.3, down from her usual 11ish - will let hematology look at it at the December visit; CBC copied to them.
3. Labs otherwise ok.
Call if fever.
